The added term is spread evenly: 4–5% of each matrix's norm, about equal for o_proj and down_proj in every layer. So the weights do not single out a dominant module. The flip proxy is informative, though. C(−1.5) pushes 0.87% of the original's confident tokens (P > 0.5) in finished answers below 0.5. That is about two to three changed choices per 300-token answer, enough to make many finished answers diverge, which fits the churn and DEV losses. C(−3) doubles the proxy to 1.9%, and the in-loop variants are much worse (3.6–6%).

So the useful measure for a cleaner variant is onset suppression per unit of flip proxy. I'll screen the two halves of C with teacher-forced passes on the same screenL texts: down_proj only first, then o_proj only. A half with most of C's onset effect (−0.44, P 0.60) but clearly less than half its flip proxy would be a candidate for a DEV generation test. If each half carries about half of each, C is as clean as this direction allows and the line closes. Plan with 10 passes: 2 screens, then a pre-registered DEV test (4 passes) against C's DEV result (48/49), then HOLDOUT only if the variant wins there.

The modular builder reproduces C(−1.5) exactly when both modules are included. The current edit is now the down_proj-only half, C_mlp(−1.5), in 7 tensors. This teacher-forced pass on screenL_texts measures its onset suppression and its flip proxy on finished answers. The pre-registered criterion is at least 2/3 of C's onset effect (about −0.29 or lower, P_onset ≤ about 0.64) with at most 1/3 of C's flip proxy (≤ 0.29%). Roughly half of each would mean no selectivity gain from the MLP half.

The down_proj-only screen is done. I'll compute the same table (onset, novel, in-loop, finished, references, P_onset) plus the flip proxy, with C(−1.5) for comparison. The pre-registered test is onset change ≤ −0.29 (or P_onset ≤ 0.64) with flip proxy ≤ 0.29%.

The down_proj-only half fails the criterion. It gives only 55% of C's onset effect (−0.24 against −0.44; P_onset 0.645 against 0.596) but keeps 77% of the flip proxy (0.67% against 0.87%). So the MLP half is the less selective part. Taken at face value, this hints that the attention (o_proj) half carries a comparable onset effect with much less collateral, perhaps 0.2–0.3% flips, though the halves need not add up.

I'll screen C_attn(−1.5), o_proj only in layers 16–22 (7 tensors), on the same texts. It passes if onset is ≤ −0.29 or P_onset ≤ 0.64 with flip ≤ 0.29%. If its onset effect is about −0.2 with a low flip proxy, a larger attention-only dose would be the natural candidate. With the 8 passes left after this, a generation test still fits: a DEV both-pass of 1,024 is 4 passes, and HOLDOUT gets the rest.
